title: One passive 13-Jupiter-mass Roche lobe cannot supply the G4466 excess in the tested thermal models
abstract: We test whether one confined dust cloud can supply the reported infrared excess of the dwarf dimmer G4466. For a circular orbit and an isotropic point star, we calculate the exact solid angle of the companion Roche lobe. A 13-Jupiter-mass companion to a 0.8-solar-mass primary can intercept at most 0.295% of the primary power. The reported dust fraction is 3.616%. A new bound from the published W3 excess gives at least 2.403% for any positive temperature mixture of the tested smooth thermal spectra, after subtraction of two nominal errors. If the cloud has no extra heat and apparent luminosity is at most four times true power, at least 50.9% of the apparent infrared emission must come from outside that lobe. The one-lobe explanation fails for primary masses of 0.4-1.2 solar masses under these assumptions. The required companion mass ratio is at least 0.04777. Two independent surface calculations agree, and three capacities reproduce old Roche tables. This is a new application of established geometry, not new photometry. Spectral features, stellar normalization, directional emission, extra power, and the assumed lobe boundary limit the result. A planet can still supply dust that escapes into a larger disc. Original code, source hashes, aggregate bounds, failure thresholds, and figures are included. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-28776c99e6ed; topic astronomy; machine hp; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: The exact Roche lobe ceiling limits passive dust power. For G4466, the spectral lower bound exceeds the capacity of a 13-Jupiter-mass lobe across the tested primary masses, even for apparent emission four times true power. The bound requires the stated smooth thermal spectra and point-source circular geometry.

The normalized thermal spectra have finite peaks. A positive mixture over temperature and the three tested beta values cannot place more bolometric power near W3 than the largest peak. Narrow spectral features are outside this family.

citations.reason: Uses published infrared fit summaries for G4466, G3768, and G2874. We add a geometric capacity test and a smooth-spectrum luminosity lower bound; no new survey measurement.
Uses the published centred WISE positions of the three dimmers as evidence against resolved blends; no new blend test.
Long dimming history motivates the dust-support question. No plate data enter our numerical bounds.
A related geometric absorption bound uses a fixed escaping source. We test confined companion dust instead.
Established Roche-lobe solid-angle irradiation relation and three independent rounded numerical checks. We do not claim the geometry as new.
Satellite debris can escape the planet and form circumstellar dust; this remains allowed by the lobe test.
Distant and retrograde satellites limit interpretation of a Roche boundary as a universal stability boundary.
